_readme.document: Regulations of the UEFA Champions League, 2025/26 season (2024-27 cycle). Enforcement date 11 September 2025.
_readme.get_the_pdf: Reader: https://documents.uefa.com/r/Regulations-of-the-UEFA-Champions-League-2025/26-Online — use its PDF download. A mirrored English PDF also exists at https://hns.family/files/documents/32483/ (Croatian FA) if the UEFA download gives you trouble.
_readme.why_2025_26: Pinned deliberately. Every paragraph reference below was read from this edition's text. Pinning the corpus keeps the gold set valid; a set tied to 'current' silently rots when UEFA renumbers.
_readme.verification: All 25 answerable questions carry paragraph-level gold read directly from the source PDF, and all 5 unanswerable items are confirmed absent from the document. Nothing left to fill in.
_readme.coverage_gap: Chapters XIII (commercial rights, Articles 69-77) and XIV (media, Articles 78-89) are the longest in the document and are not represented in this set. Your index will contain a large body of text no question ever probes. Worth naming in the write-up — and worth adding a question or two later if you want coverage.
_readme.paragraph_spread: Gold spans 22 distinct paragraphs across 14 articles. Keep it that way if you add questions — two questions on one paragraph means one is redundant.
_readme.keep_away_from_claude_code: Build the eval runner against a 2-3 question dummy file, then drop this file in afterwards.
_readme.corpus_checksum: Confirm you have the right file: title 'Regulations of the UEFA Champions League', 2024-27 Cycle, 2025/26 Season. Paragraph 31.04 states no club may have more than 25 players on List A. Paragraph 31.12 gives the List B birth cutoff as 1 January 2004. Paragraph 11.03 awards 50 gold medals. If those three match, every gold reference lines up.

answerable.question: How many players can a club put on its main squad list?
answerable.goldAnswer: Maximum 25 on List A.

answerable.question: How many places in the main squad list are reserved for locally trained players, and how many of those can be association-trained?
answerable.goldAnswer: At least eight reserved; no more than four of those may be association-trained.
answerable.note: Two-part answer. Checks the model returns the whole rule, not half of it.

answerable.question: A club registers a new player during the qualifying phase and that takes List A to 26 names. What must it do?
answerable.goldAnswer: Remove a previously registered player to bring List A back to 25.

answerable.question: What is the minimum number of goalkeepers a club must register?
answerable.goldAnswer: At least two on List A, at least three across List A and List B combined.

answerable.question: What are the age and tenure conditions for putting a young player on List B?
answerable.goldAnswer: Born on or after 1 January 2004, and since his 15th birthday eligible for the club for an uninterrupted two years or three consecutive years, with at most one loan of up to a year to a club in the same association. Players aged 16 qualify with two uninterrupted years at the club.

answerable.question: Can a club add new players to its squad after the league phase ends?
answerable.goldAnswer: Yes, a maximum of three new eligible players, by 5 February 2026.
answerable.note: 32.02 adds exceptions for calendar-year championships (up to four or five). A thorough answer reaches it; a shallow one stops at three.

answerable.question: How many substitutions is a team allowed during a match?
answerable.goldAnswer: Up to five substitutes, plus a sixth in knockout extra time, using a maximum of three stoppages in play (one extra in extra time).

answerable.question: What happens if a knockout tie is level after both legs?
answerable.goldAnswer: Two 15-minute periods of extra time, then a penalty shoot-out if still level.

answerable.question: What share of stadium capacity has to be made available to visiting supporters, and is there a price limit?
answerable.goldAnswer: At least 5% of UEFA spectator capacity, priced no higher than comparable home-supporter adult tickets and capped at €50.

answerable.question: How many medals do the winning and losing finalists receive?
answerable.goldAnswer: 50 gold to the winners, 50 silver to the runners-up.

answerable.question: If a club only has six locally trained players available, what happens to the size of its squad?
answerable.goldAnswer: The maximum registrable on List A is reduced accordingly.
answerable.note: A model may retrieve 31.04 and recite the quota instead of the consequence. Good near-miss.

answerable.question: Two clubs finish the league phase on the same number of points. How is the higher position decided?
answerable.goldAnswer: Ten criteria applied in order, starting with goal difference and ending with club coefficient.
answerable.note: A single paragraph containing a ten-item ordered list. If your chunker splits it, the model will return a partial ordering that looks plausible and is wrong. Best structural test in the set.

answerable.question: A player is sent off in the last league phase match. Does that suspension carry into the knockout rounds?
answerable.goldAnswer: Yes. A sending-off brings an automatic suspension for the next match, and pending suspensions carry forward to the next round, subject to the exceptions in 63.04.
answerable.note: Paragraph numbers cross-read from the parallel Europa League Article 63, which explicitly cites 63.04. Spot-check against the CL text — this is the least directly verified of the 24.

answerable.question: A club's first-choice goalkeeper is injured for two months. Can they bring in a replacement, and does the replacement have to be locally trained?
answerable.goldAnswer: Yes, if the injury lasts at least 30 days. The replacement does not have to be locally trained even if the replaced goalkeeper was.
answerable.note: The 'does not have to be locally trained' clause sits deep in a long paragraph and is easy to drop.

answerable.question: How long must an outfield player be out before he can be replaced, and is that the same threshold as for a goalkeeper?
answerable.goldAnswer: 60 days for an outfield player versus 30 for a goalkeeper. Outfield replacement is also limited to one player, up to matchday 6.
answerable.note: Deliberate distractor pair with a14 — both live in 31.14, so the model must pick the right sub-paragraph, not the right article. Strongest chunk-granularity test here.

answerable.question: Two clubs turn up with clashing shirts. Who has to change — and is the answer different in the final?
answerable.goldAnswer: As a rule the home team changes, decided by the referee with the match delegate and UEFA administration. In the final the rule reverses: the designated away team wears alternative colours.
answerable.note: 40.03 contradicts 40.02 for one specific fixture. A model that retrieves a single chunk will state the general rule confidently and be wrong about the final. The best hallucination trap in the set — and it is a real rule, not a contrived one.

answerable.question: Can two clubs owned by the same investment group both play in this competition?
answerable.goldAnswer: No, where one entity has control or decisive influence over both. If two clubs fail the criteria only one is admitted, chosen by competition prestige, then domestic ranking, then association access-list position.
answerable.note: Conditional answer with a tie-break order, spanning two paragraphs.

answerable.question: A match is abandoned at half-time and resumed the following day. Which players can take the field?
answerable.goldAnswer: The same players and listed substitutes as at suspension. A player unable to restart may be replaced by a listed substitute, counting as a substitution. Sanctions already imposed stand and sendings-off cannot be replaced.
answerable.note: 28.01(b) covers resumption at a later date with different rules — a natural distractor sitting in the same article.

answerable.question: Does a player's passport determine whether he counts toward the domestic development requirement?
answerable.goldAnswer: No. Both definitions apply irrespective of nationality; what matters is registration history between 15 and 21.
answerable.note: Avoids 'homegrown', 'locally trained', 'nationality'. The answering phrase is buried mid-paragraph in a wall of text, which is exactly why keyword search should miss it. One of four questions the hybrid-vs-vector experiment turns on.

answerable.question: A player left off both squad lists picks up a ban. Can he sit it out while unregistered?
answerable.goldAnswer: No. Only players registered via List A or B can validly serve pending suspensions.
answerable.note: A one-sentence paragraph. Short chunks are easy to lose in a large index.

answerable.question: After a defeat, is the head coach personally required to speak to broadcasters, and how quickly must the press conference start?
answerable.goldAnswer: Not personally for the flash interview — 80.01(d) requires the head coach OR a key player for at least one post-match super-flash interview. But 80.02 requires both clubs to make their head coach available at the post-match press conference, which must start no later than 20 minutes after the final whistle.
answerable.note: Two-part answer split across two paragraphs that pull in opposite directions: one says the coach is substitutable, the other does not. Retrieving only 80.01(d) yields a confident 'no'; retrieving only 80.02 yields a confident 'yes'. Near-misses to watch for: 79.01 (pre-match press conference) and 6.01(j) (player of the match available for interview).

answerable.question: Can a club choose which ball is used for its home fixtures?
answerable.goldAnswer: Only in the qualifying phase, where the home club provides balls meeting IFAB and UEFA Equipment Regulations. From the play-offs onwards the official UEFA match ball is mandatory.
answerable.note: Answer is conditional on competition stage. A model retrieving only 50.02 will say a flat no and miss the qualifying-phase case.

answerable.question: Does Liverpool's registered squad satisfy the locally trained player requirement?
answerable.note: Needs 31.04 AND GetSquad. Assert usedTool == true.

answerable.question: Manchester United are short on club-trained players. How many can they actually register on List A as things stand?
answerable.note: Needs 31.08, the reduction rule, applied to a real count. Hardest of the three: reciting the quota is not an answer.

answerable.question: Real Madrid have registered the goalkeepers shown in their squad. Are they compliant on that front?
answerable.note: Simplest tool case. Also checks the agent does not over-retrieve.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum proportion of revenue a club may spend on wages and transfer fees?
unanswerable.note: CONFIRMED safe. Articles 65-68 cover match revenue and distribution, not spending limits. 4.01(c) and 6.01(g) only cross-reference the Club Licensing and Financial Sustainability Regulations.

unanswerable.question: How many non-homegrown players can a club register in the Premier League?
unanswerable.note: Different governing body. Sharpest item here — topically adjacent to a02, so a model that pattern-matches on 'homegrown' will answer confidently with UEFA's numbers.

unanswerable.question: How many matches is a player banned for after spitting at an opponent?
unanswerable.note: CONFIRMED safe. Article 63 covers card-based suspensions only; 63.01 defers serious offences to the UEFA Control, Ethics and Disciplinary Body. No offence tariff table in this document.

unanswerable.question: When does the summer transfer window close in Spain?
unanswerable.note: National association matter. Nothing in the document covers it.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum permitted temperature of the dressing room?
unanswerable.note: CONFIRMED safe. Chapter V covers stadiums, pitches, artificial turf, floodlights and technologies — no dressing-room environmental spec. Sounds exactly like a clause this document might contain, which is the point.
